questions.question: What is the full form of FICCI?

options.text: Federation of Indian Chamber of Commerce & Industry
Federation of International Chamber of Commerce & Industry
Federation of Indonesian Chamber of Commerce & Industry
Federation of Iranian Chamber of Commerce & Industry

questions.solution:
• The full form of FICCI is Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce & Industry.
 
• It is an association of Indian business organisations and was established in 1927.
 
• It is a not-for-profit and non-governmental organisation.

questions.question: What is the meaning of National income?
questions.solution:
• National income is the total amount of income of a country in a year from all the economic activities.
 
• It comprises payments made to all the resources in the form of rents, profits, wages, and interests.

questions.question: Under which article does the President declare a 'Financial Emergency' in India?
questions.solution:
• Financial Emergency under the Article 360, is declared by the President when there is an economic situation which could threaten the financial stability of India.
 
• National Emergency under the Article 352, is declared by the President on the basis of armed rebellion or external aggression in India.
 
• State Emergency under the Article 356, can be declared in any state of India, except J&K, on the recommendation of the state Governor. This is also known as the ‘President’s rule’.

questions.question: Other than 'Right to life' which other right is mentioned in the article 21 of Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
• The Article 21 of the Indian Constitution secures two rights, which are Right to Life and Right to Personal Liberty.
 
• The article reads as ‘No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to a procedure established by law’.

questions.question:
Arrange the following rulers in the correct order according to the period of their rule.

1. Qutbuddin Aibak

2. Ghiyasuddin Balban

3. Shamsuddin Iltutmish

4. Razia
questions.solution: The correct order of the Sultans of the Delhi Sultanate is: Qutbuddin Aibak (1206-1210), Shamsuddin Iltutmish (1211-1236), Razia Sultan (1236-1240), and Ghiyasuddin Balban (1266-1287).

questions.question: In which year did the Chauri Chaura incident happen?
questions.solution:
• The Chauri Chaura incident took place on February 5, 1922, at Chauri Chaura in the Gorakhpur district of present-day U.P.
 
• A large group of participants of the Non-Cooperation movement and protesters clashed with the police who opened fire.

questions.question: Through which of the following Continents Amazon river flows?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Amazon river**__ is the** largest river** in the world in terms of discharge volume of water and also the longest river in South America.
 
• It flows through the continent __**South America **__and countries Brazil, Colombia, Peru, Venezuela, Bolivia, Ecuador, and Guyana.

questions.question: ‘Maitri' and 'Dakshin Gangotri' are the research stations of India in which continent?
questions.solution:
• Dakshin Gangotri was the first Indian scientific base station situated in Antarctica. It is a part of the Indian Antarctic Programme and is situated 2500 km from the South Pole. Currently, it is being used as a transit camp and a supply base.
 
• Maitri is the second permanent research station of India in Antarctica which is also a part of the Indian Antarctic Programme.

questions.question: Which among the following is not an example of terrestrial habitat?
questions.solution: Terrestrial habitats are those which are found on land such as deserts, grasslands, forests, wetlands, and shorelines. It also comprises of man-made habitats such as towns, cities, and farms.

questions.question: A specific function of light energy in the process of photosynthesis is to ________.
questions.solution:
• A specific function of light energy in the process of photosynthesis is to activate chlorophyll.
 
• Photosynthesis is a process through which plants synthesize nutrients in the presence of sunlight from water and carbon dioxide.

questions.question: In a human's heart the bicuspid valve is situated between ________.
questions.solution:
• The bicuspid valve or the left atrioventricular valve or the mitral valve is a valve that lies between the left ventricle and left atrium.
 
• It has 2 flaps in the heart.
 
• When the left ventricle contracts, the bicuspid valve closes during systole and when the left atrium contracts, the valve opens during diastole and blood flows through it.

questions.question: What is the process of transferring of charge from a charged object to the earth called?
questions.solution:
__Explanation:__

There are two types of charges found in nature -

 
• Positive charge
 
• Negative charge

 

Properties of charges:

 
• Like charges (same charges) repel each other.
 
• Unlike charges (different charges) attract each other.

 

When two objects are rubbed against each other, they develop charges

Earthing: The process of transfer of charge from a charged object to the Earth is known as Earthing.

 
• An electric discharge is the transmission and release of electricity through a medium such as gas in the applied electric field.
 
• **Lightning **is caused because of the build-up of **electrostatic charges** in the clouds.

questions.question: If the reflecting surface of a spherical mirror is curved inwards, it is called ________ mirror.
questions.solution:
• If the reflecting surface of a spherical mirror is curved inwards, it is called a concave mirror.
 
• If the reflecting surface of a spherical mirror is curved outwards, it is called a convex mirror.
 
• A plane mirror has a flat reflective surface.
 
• An optical lens with a positive focal length is a plano-convex lens.

questions.question: Integrated Circuits are made up of which of the following?
questions.solution:
• An IC or Integrated Circuit, also known as microchip, chip, or microelectronic circuit is an assembly of electronic components which are fabricated as a single unit.
 
• The active and passive devices such as transistors and resistors and their interconnections are built on a thin substrate of silicon, a semiconductor material.

questions.question: ________ is a lustrous non-metal.
questions.solution:
• Iodine is a lustrous non-metal.
 
• It shows lustre like metals and has lower electronegativity like other non-metals.
 
• It shows the properties of both metals and non-metals.

questions.question: Soda water has a pH value ________.
questions.solution:
• Soda water, which also known as carbonated water is acidic in nature.
 
• It has a pH value

questions.question: What are the substances that are broken down by biological process called?
questions.solution:
• The substances that are broken down by the biological process are called biodegradable substances.
 
• The substances such as plastics and metals which cannot be broken down by the biological process are called non-biodegradable substances.
 
• Fossils are the preserved traces, remains, or impression of any living thing that once existed in the past geological age.
 
• Chemically inactive substances are known as inert.

questions.question: Which among the following schemes has the objective to promote apprenticeship training and increase the engagement of apprentices to 50 lakh by 2020?
questions.solution:
The National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme is a scheme which was launched by the government on 19 August 2016. Its objectives are:

 
• To promote apprenticeship training.
 
• To increase the engagement of apprentices to 50 lakh by 2020.
 
• To incentivize employers who want to engage apprentices.

questions.question: Who discovered the nucleus of a cell?
questions.solution:
• Scottish botanist Robert Brown discovered the nucleus of a cell in 1831.
 
• A nucleus is an organelle found in the eukaryotic cells and are enclosed by the membranes.
 
• The main function of the nucleus is to store the cell's DNA.

questions.question: Which team won the FIFA Confederations Cup 2017?
questions.solution: Germany won the FIFA Confederations Cup 2017. The match was held as a prelude to the FIFA World Cup 2018 from 17th June to 2nd July 2017 in Russia.

questions.question: In which of the following art expressions, is the painting generally done by pen?
questions.solution:
• Kalamkari is a type of hand painting done on cotton or silk fabric. It is produced in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
 
• Rangoli is an art form in which patterns are created on the floor using dry flour, flower petals, colored sand, or colored rice.
 
• Phad is a Rajasthani folk painting.

questions.question: Which hockey player has been awarded 2017 Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award?
questions.solution:
• Sardara Singh was awarded Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award 2017 for Hockey.
 
• The award is the highest sporting honour of India.

questions.question: Who is the author of the book named “The Origin of Species”?
questions.solution: Charles Darwin is the author of the book named “The Origin of Species”. ** Author** ** Book**

questions.question: Yudh Abhyas is a joint military training exercise of Indian and ________ armies.
questions.solution:
• Yudh Abhyas is a joint military training exercise of Indian and US armies.
 
• It is taking place at Chaubatia in the Almora district of Uttarakhand. 
 
• This exercise began on September 16, 2018, and is a major bilateral defence cooperation endeavour between the US and India.
 
• It is also one of the longest running training exercises.

questions.question: Which is a joint venture and campaign for mutual peace and development of diplomatic and cultural relations between India and Pakistan?
questions.solution:
• Aman ki Asha is a joint venture and campaign for mutual peace and development of diplomatic and cultural relations between India and Pakistan.
 
• It was jointly started by 2 leading media houses, The Times of India, from India and The Jang Group of Pakistan on 1 January, 2010.
